channel.title: The Full Bloom Blog
channel.description: Practical insights, clinical wisdom, and honest reflections on mental health, relationships, and living well, from the therapists at Full Bloom Counseling in Denver, Colorado.

item.title: 300 Days of Sunshine and Still Sad in November
item.description: Colorado is sunny, and winter can still flatten you. A Denver therapist on seasonal depression, the 300-days myth, light boxes, and when to get help.

item.title: What Is Internal Family Systems (IFS)? Parts Work, Explained in Plain English
item.description: Managers, exiles, firefighters and Self. A Denver therapist who uses IFS daily explains how parts work, what a session looks like, and who it helps.

item.title: You Said Yes Before You Even Decided: Notes for Recovering People Pleasers
item.description: The automatic yes, the guilt after a no, and the resentment in between. A Denver therapist on where people pleasing comes from and what actually helps.

item.title: Why Family Vacations Bring Out the Worst in Us (Even the Good Ones)
item.description: Months of planning, and the meltdown still hits by 2 p.m. A Denver family therapist, writing from Disneyland, on why trips get tense and what helps.

item.title: The Mental Load: Why You’re Exhausted When Nothing Is Technically Wrong
item.description: Tracking every appointment, birthday and permission slip is real work. A Denver therapist on the mental load, why rest doesn’t fix it, and what does.

item.title: Nobody Sends Flowers After a Miscarriage
item.description: Miscarriage ends 10 to 20 percent of known pregnancies, and most people grieve it quietly. A Denver perinatal therapist on that grief and when to get support.

item.title: Finally Diagnosed With ADHD as an Adult. Now What?
item.description: More than half of adults with ADHD were diagnosed after 18. A Denver therapist on the mix of relief and grief that follows, and what helps next.

item.title: When Your Teen Dreads Going Back to School
item.description: Sunday night stomachaches, calls from the nurse, a kid who used to like school. A Denver family therapist on teen school anxiety and what actually helps.

item.title: How Long Does Therapy Take? A Denver Therapist’s Honest Answer
item.description: How many sessions until therapy works? Real research ranges, what speeds progress up, and how you’ll know it’s working: honest answers, no dodging.

item.title: Online Therapy in Colorado: Does Virtual Therapy Actually Work?
item.description: Is virtual therapy as effective as in-person? What the research says, who it fits best, and what an online session actually looks like.

item.title: Therapy in Cherry Creek & Glendale: A Local Guide
item.description: Looking for a therapist close to home? A local guide to starting therapy near Cherry Creek and Glendale: what to expect, how to choose, and how to begin.

item.title: How Much Does Therapy Cost in Denver? A Transparent Guide
item.description: Real numbers, no guesswork: what therapy costs in Denver, why rates vary so much, and the strategies that make it more affordable.

item.title: Does Insurance Cover Therapy in Colorado? Superbills, Explained
item.description: What out-of-network actually means, how superbills work, and the exact questions to ask your insurance company before your first session.

item.title: How to Find the Right Therapist in Denver (Without the Overwhelm)
item.description: Looking for a therapist in Denver but not sure where to start? A practical guide on finding the right fit, without the analysis paralysis.

item.title: Therapy for Men in Denver: Why It’s Different and Why It Works
item.description: Therapy built for men isn’t softer. It’s sharper. Mark Whitney on what makes men’s therapy work and what actually changes when it does.
